payload.command:
MILES EXECUTIVE DIRECTIVE

Improve the Command Intent Planner.

The planner must classify the overall objective before selecting a provider.

Priority order:

1. Executive directives
2. System improvement
3. Engineering tasks
4. Multi-step workflows
5. Single connector actions

Do not classify based on isolated keywords.

If a command contains multiple objectives, create a workflow rather than selecting a single connector.

Examples:

"Run an Executive Integration Audit"
→ EXECUTIVE_AUDIT workflow

"Improve MILES OS"
→ ENGINEERING_IMPROVEMENT workflow

"Maintain MILES going forward"
→ AUTONOMOUS_IMPROVEMENT workflow

Only classify as WEBSITE_REVIEW when the primary objective is actually reviewing the website.

After implementing this change, validate using:

- Improve MILES OS.
- Run Executive Integration Audit.
- Review the website.
- Check ORION health.

Show the selected workflow, provider, and action for each test.

MILES EXECUTIVE DIRECTIVE

The command pipeline is functioning correctly.

Current flow:

CEO Command
→ Intent Planner
→ Business Operations Queue
→ Business Bridge
→ Task Queue
→ Execution Service
→ Connector
→ Executive Response

The remaining weakness is Intent Planning.

Currently the planner selects a connector too early.

Example:

"Improve MILES OS"

is incorrectly classified as an ORION action.

Instead, implement a two-stage planning architecture.

Stage 1

Determine the command intent.

Possible intents include:

• Operational Request
• Executive Directive
• Engineering Improvement
• Self Improvement
• Executive Audit
• Business Operation
• Connector Operation
• Research
• Autonomous Improvement

Stage 2

Build a workflow from the intent.

Only after the workflow is built should providers/connectors be selected.

Examples

"Check ORION Health"

Intent:
Operational Request

Workflow:
ORION_HEALTH

Provider:
ORION

----------------------------------

"Improve MILES OS"

Intent:
Engineering Improvement

Workflow:
ENGINEERING_IMPROVEMENT

Providers:
Engineering
Planner
Execution
Memory

----------------------------------

"Review Website"

Intent:
Business Operation

Workflow:
WEBSITE_REVIEW

Provider:
Website

----------------------------------

"Run Executive Integration Audit"

Intent:
Executive Audit

Workflow:
EXECUTIVE_AUDIT

Providers:
Engineering
ORION
Connectors
Runtime
Memory

Requirements

• Do not replace existing architecture.
• Extend CommandIntentPlannerService.
• Create an IntentClassifier layer.
• Create a WorkflowPlanner layer.
• Preserve all existing APIs.
• Preserve existing connector execution.
• Validate all existing commands.
• Document the new workflow.

When complete:

Run validation against:

Check ORION Health

Improve MILES OS

Review Website

Run Executive Integration Audit

Maintain MILES going forward

Show:

Intent
Workflow
Providers
Execution Plan

Then permanently adopt this architecture.

payload.command:
The current planner is still keyword routing.

Replace keyword routing with hierarchical intent classification.

Planning order must become:

1. Executive Directive
2. Engineering Improvement
3. Self Improvement
4. Executive Audit
5. Multi-step Workflow
6. Business Operation
7. Connector Operation

Connector selection happens LAST.

Never select ORION simply because the command contains the word ORION.

Never select Website because the command mentions website.

Never select Instantly because the command mentions campaigns.

First determine the overall objective.

Then build a workflow.

Then determine providers.

This replaces keyword-first routing.

payload.command:
MILES EXECUTIVE DIRECTIVE

BUILD 042

Runtime Execution Trace Engine

Objective

Implement a runtime execution tracing capability for MILES OS.

Current engineering analysis relies primarily on static file inspection.

MILES must now observe and report the actual runtime execution path of every operation.

Requirements

Instrument the active runtime.

For every operation, capture and report:

1. Operation ID
2. Timestamp
3. Command received
4. Planner
   - intent
   - workflow
   - provider
   - connector
   - action
5. ExecutionService
   - input
   - output
   - routing decision
6. ConnectorManager
   - connector requested
   - connector selected
7. Connector
   - task received
   - task dispatched
8. Builder
   - action received
   - capability matched
9. Service
   - service invoked
   - execution result
10. Completion
    - duration
    - success/failure
    - recovery attempts

For every transition record:

• Input
• Output
• Decision
• Evidence

Store every trace as structured JSON.

Maintain a rolling history of the most recent execution traces.

Validation

Run live traces for:

- Improve MILES OS
- Check ORION Health
- Review Website
- Executive Integration Audit

Demonstrate that every stage preserves the planned action unless an intentional transformation occurs.

If any stage changes the action, provider, workflow, or connector:

Report:

- exact file
- exact function
- reason
- evidence

Do not rely solely on source code inspection.

Use the active running runtime.

Deliverables

- Runtime Trace Engine
- Runtime Trace Repository
- Executive Trace Report
- Validation Results

Do not modify production routing logic unless explicitly approved.

This capability becomes part of MILES Developer Mode.

BUILD 043

Runtime Instrumentation Layer

Objective

Implement runtime instrumentation for the active MILES execution pipeline.

This is not an engineering proposal.

This is an implementation.

Requirements

Instrument the running system.

Add trace events at the following locations:

1. MilesCommandCenter
2. CommandIntentPlannerService
3. ExecutionService
4. ConnectorManager
5. Every Connector
6. BuilderService
7. Final Service Execution

Each stage shall emit a structured trace event containing:

- operationId
- timestamp
- stage
- file
- function
- provider
- connector
- workflow
- intent
- action
- input
- output
- executionTimeMs

Store traces in memory and write them to:

DATA/runtime_traces/

Create one JSON file per operation.

Validation

Run these commands through the live runtime:

- Improve MILES OS
- Check ORION Health
- Review Website

For each command produce a complete execution trace showing every stage.

Do not produce a proposal.

Implement the instrumentation.

Do not replace existing architecture.

Integrate into the current production pipeline.

Return the runtime trace files and a summary report.

• writeFile
• fs.writeFile

• createWriteStream
• patch generation
• replacement generation
• code generation
• source generation
• template generation

Also search for services named similarly to:

CodeWriter

ReplacementGenerator
PatchEngine
PatchGenerator
CodeGenerator
EngineeringWriter
RuntimeWriter
TemplateEngine

- file
- function
- purpose
- whether it is currently invoked by EngineeringImprovementService

3. If no, explicitly state:

"The current MILES runtime has no code-generation engine. EngineeringImprovementService can only generate engineering proposals."

Do not recommend changes.

Return evidence only.

This service must not invoke EngineeringImprovementService.

This service must not generate plans, proposals, or implementation packages.

The service shall:

1. Receive a requested action.

3. Record:
   - incoming action
   - planner output
   - provider
   - connector
   - builder action
   - service selected
   - service actually executed
4. Produce a JSON dispatch trace.

After creating the service, register a new Builder action:

RUNTIME_DISPATCH_DIAGNOSTIC

Validate by executing:

RUNTIME_DISPATCH_DIAGNOSTIC

Expected output:

A runtime dispatch trace showing the actual execution path without entering EngineeringImprovementService.

If the diagnostic itself enters EngineeringImprovementService, report that as a routing defect.

BUILD 050

Runtime Dispatch Instrumentation

Objective

Instrument the live runtime dispatcher.

This is NOT an engineering improvement.

This is NOT a proposal.

This is NOT a planning task.

Requirements

Modify the runtime dispatcher itself to emit a dispatch trace for every request.

For every command log:

REQUEST RECEIVED

↓

PLANNER OUTPUT

↓

PROVIDER

↓

CONNECTOR

↓

BUILDER ACTION

↓

SERVICE NAME

↓

SERVICE FILE

↓

METHOD INVOKED

↓

RESULT

Write each trace to:

DATA/runtime_dispatch/runtime_dispatch.log

Do not execute EngineeringImprovementService to generate this report.

The instrumentation must occur inside the dispatcher so that every future request automatically records its execution path.

Success Criteria

After installation, execute:

STATUS

The runtime log must show the complete dispatch path from command receipt through the final service invocation.
